winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一

clip_research.source_claim: Tencent said AI spending peaked in Q3, and Morningstar expects revenue to catch up with spending by 2028, so the market is a bit too bearish.
clip_research.public_baseline: Morningstar/Dow Jones reports Tencent management said AI capex will remain near peak levels through 2026 and into 2027 before easing in 2028; Q3 capex payments jumped 225% to RMB65.1bn and adjusted operating margin narrowed to 33% from 38%.
clip_research.surprise_gap: The 'peaked in Q3' framing conflicts with public reporting that spending stays near peak through 2027; the 2028 catch-up is a forecast, not a reported fact.

evidence.fact: Tencent spending peaked in Q3; revenue catches up by 2028; market a bit too bearish.

briefs.speaker: Lorraine Tan
briefs.speaker_context: Director of Asia Equity Research at Morningstar
briefs.current_title: 晨星Lorraine Tan：腾讯豪赌AI牺牲利润，市场是否过度悲观？

subtitles.zh: 从腾讯财报可以看出，这些科技公司确实在大力投入，愿意牺牲利润率，也拖累了利润增长，对吧？
subtitles.en: you're seeing from the Tencent earnings that these tech companies are really aggressively spending and willing to sacrifice margins as well as stalling profit growth, right?

subtitles.zh: 你对这些财报有什么看法？
subtitles.en: I mean, what is your reaction to some of these earnings?

subtitles.zh: 其实腾讯的情况基本符合我们的预期，原因是这些公司正处于建设阶段，而在建设阶段
subtitles.en: Yeah, so actually what happened at Tencent is largely within our expectation, and I think the reason for that is that it's the companies are in a build-out phase, and a build-out phase

subtitles.zh: 你确实会预期在收入赶上支出之前，会有资金流出。
subtitles.en: you do expect the outflows to be there before the revenue catches up with the spending.

subtitles.zh: 所以我们确实预计，大多数行业到2028年收入会开始赶上支出。
subtitles.en: So we actually do anticipate from most of the industry that we will see that sort of catch up, revenue start to catch up with the spending by 2028.

subtitles.zh: 那么接下来，你会开始看到这些公司的压力有所减轻。
subtitles.en: So what will happen then is that you will start to see that pressure start to reduce some of these companies.

subtitles.zh: 我认为腾讯确实提到，他们认为支出在第三季度已经见顶。
subtitles.en: And I think Tencent did mention that they think that the spending has peaked in the third quarter.

subtitles.zh: 好的。市场是否过于悲观？
subtitles.en: Okay. Is the market too bearish?

subtitles.zh: 我们认为有点过于悲观，原因是变现将会实现。
subtitles.en: We think it's a little bit too bearish, and the reason we say that is that the monetization will come through.

subtitles.zh: 你知道，KPX之所以意外上行，是因为所有芯片成本都上升了。
subtitles.en: The reason, you know, the KPX has been surprising at the upside is because all the chip costs went up.

subtitles.zh: 这些公司目前正投入支出，这是好事。但当我们开始看到芯片价格回落，输入成本开始缓解，我认为这也是我们更乐观的部分原因。
subtitles.en: These companies are committed to the spending right now, which is a good thing. Yes, but when we're starting to see those chip prices come off, so the input costs start to ease, and I think that's part of the reason why we're, you know, I g

subtitles.zh: 更乐观，而且我们确实看到这些公司的价值。
subtitles.en: more optimistic, and we do see value in these companies.

Operating rule: 二极管法则
- A candidate is usable only if one emotion pole is unmistakable and emotion_tension is at least 8/10.
- The six permitted poles are: unexpected reversal, pleasant surprise, strong doubt, finally-someone-said-it candor, verified words-versus-actions contrast, and fact-based pride in a Chinese comparative advantage.
- Do not split the emotion across several mild ideas. Pick one pole and push it to the factual limit.
- A question mark is not emotion. "前景如何", "回报路径在哪", "能否实现", "面临哪些挑战", "回报存疑", and "释放什么信号" score at most 4 unless they contain a concrete contradiction or consequence.

Angle rules:
- surprise_reversal: state the familiar baseline, then expose the source claim that reverses it. Do not turn a baseline contrast into "改口" unless research.position_change.supported is true with at least two independent sources.
- outsider_candor: use only when a foreign institution/expert says something unusually direct. Keep the identity contrast in evidence_basis and viewer_reaction, then realize it in final copy by placing the specific surprising claim against its consequence. Never literally output 外资策略师、外资首席、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话, or 西方机构承认.
- words_vs_actions: use only when research.words_vs_actions.supported is true and independent_source_count is at least 2. Show the two exact sides in question form. Never directly call anyone a liar.
- china_advantage: use only when research.china_advantage.supported is true. Put the concrete Chinese advantage or the foreign competitor's forced response in the foreground. The emotional direction must favor China.
- authority_breaks_consensus: the authority must be recognizable to a China audience, or be labeled by a meaningful role. Do not lead with an obscure romanized name.
- concrete_stakes: expose a specific number, forced choice, consequence, or who gains/loses. Generic importance is not a stake.

Writing rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Produce exactly four candidates per clip and use at least three different angle_id values when the evidence permits.
- Each candidate has exactly three short title lines. Think cover blocks, not a newspaper sentence.
- Ideal line lengths are 3-10, 4-12, and 5-14 Chinese characters. Full title is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- The title must reveal enough familiar context to create a small information gap, then withhold the explanation supplied by the video.
- Prefer concrete verbs and consequences: 逼急、藏不住、说透、砍半. Use only when facts support them. "改口" requires research.position_change.supported with two independent sources; words-versus-actions phrases require research.words_vs_actions.supported with two independent sources.
- Do not mechanically copy examples or proper nouns from instructions. Derive every noun, number, actor, and comparison from this clip and its evidence card.
- angle_id, emotion_pole, and viewer_reaction are private editorial metadata. Never copy their wording into title or title_lines.
- Final cover structure should be [specific subject] / [unexpected fact or comparison] / [concrete unresolved consequence], not [speaker category] / [editorial label] / [topic].
- If a person or institution is genuinely recognizable, use its verified proper name. If it is not recognizable, omit the identity and lead with the subject and fact; do not replace it with generic labels such as 外资策略师 or 海外专家.
- For names and technical terms, use only the current clip's verified title_label. Never use official_zh/legal company names as cover copy, and never invent a Chinese transliteration when title_label is empty or English.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is a source label, not the expert or actor. Company legal suffixes do not belong in a title.
- For China-related clips, never attack China or imply national decline. Favor confidence, competence, policy room, industrial strength, cost advantage, talent, resilience, and competitors being forced to respond.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.

- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.

briefs.speaker: Gracie Lin
briefs.speaker_context: OKX, Regional CEO for Singapore and Australia, Head of VIP Growth
briefs.current_title: OKX林慧仪：AI估值高企，零售20%配置是信心还是泡沫？

subtitles.zh: 因为这与宣传时的差距很大。是的，我也很惊讶。
subtitles.en: Because that's quite a gap from what it was marketed with. Yeah, that was surprising to me as well.

subtitles.zh: 尽管关于技术不确定性和AI公司能否实现潜力的讨论很多，但乐观情绪似乎依然存在。
subtitles.en: It seems like the bullishness has stayed, even though there's so much talk about the uncertainty behind technology, behind whether the AI companies will realize the potential

subtitles.zh: 以及人们对它们的高期望。看起来，散户市场参与者肯定仍然非常感兴趣。
subtitles.en: and the high expectations that people have set for them. And it seems like, I don't know, the retail investors definitely are still very interested.

subtitles.zh: 机构市场参与者也没有离场。所以情况就是这样。
subtitles.en: The institutional investors are not going anywhere. So that's kind of what it's been.

subtitles.zh: 嗯，担忧在于价格可能已反映了完美预期。这很难想象，对吧？
subtitles.en: Well, the concern is that it is possibly price for perfection. It's so hard to imagine, right?

subtitles.zh: 在AI领域，完美是什么？因为我们已经看到了。
subtitles.en: What perfection is when it comes to AI? Because we've seen it.

subtitles.zh: 公司开始真正将AI工具整合到工作流程中，大概才一年左右。
subtitles.en: It's only been, well, I think maybe about a year now that companies have started to really integrate AI tools into our workflows.

subtitles.zh: 最初，我们以为这只是生产力驱动，只会提高生产力。
subtitles.en: And initially, we thought it would just be productivity drive. It would just improve productivity.

subtitles.zh: 但它所做的远不止这些。我们现在看到，它不仅能替代，还能增强人类员工的工作。
subtitles.en: But what has done is so much more than that. We are now seeing that it can really not just replace but also augment what some of our human employees are doing.

subtitles.zh: 然后，人类员工可以变得更高效，真正将业务提升到新的水平。
subtitles.en: And then our human employees can then start to be more productive and start to really bring the business to the next level.

subtitles.zh: 所以如果我们设想，每家公司都大规模这样做，那么全球经济将如何再上一个台阶。
subtitles.en: So if we think about, if each company does this at scale, then you think about how the global economy is going to then move a step up.

subtitles.zh: 然后你可以想象，其中有多少会回流到推动创新的公司，并让这些工具为我们所用。
subtitles.en: Then you can think about how much of that is going to then go back into companies and traffic that are driving that innovation and are making the tools available for us.

subtitles.zh: 这存在很大的先发优势。因为他们很早就达到了规模，我认为这是乐观的好理由。
subtitles.en: And there's a lot of that first mover advantage. And because they've already come to the scale so early on, I think that's a good reason to be optimistic.

subtitles.zh: 对许多市场参与者来说，这也关乎回报率以及她将如何看待。
subtitles.en: I think for a lot of investors, it's also about ROI and how she will see that.

subtitles.zh: 我们谈到零售市场参与者，20%配置给零售市场参与者。
subtitles.en: We talk about retail investors, 20% allocation to retail investors.

subtitles.zh: 这是相当大的数额。这是否会改变格局？我认为这意味着他们非常有信心，不仅仅依赖机构来看到
subtitles.en: That's quite a big amount. Is that a game changer? I think it means that they're very confident that they're not just relying on institutions to see the power

subtitles.zh: 他们带给市场的力量。他们相信，零售市场参与者看到人工智能开始在他们自己的生活中真正发挥作用
subtitles.en: of what they bring to market. They are believing that retail investors who see how AI is starting to really play a role in their own lives

subtitles.zh: 以及在他们家人、朋友的生活中，会真正相信它，然后也会将部分配置投入其中。
subtitles.en: and in their families' lives, their friends' lives are going to really believe in it and also then put some of their allocation into a traffic.

subtitles.zh: 对我来说，这表明公司对他们将继续带给市场的东西极其自信。
subtitles.en: To me, that suggests that the company is extremely confident of what they are going to be continuing to bring to market.

subtitles.zh: 很棒。
subtitles.en: Great thing.

briefs.speaker: Gracie Lin
briefs.speaker_context: OKX, Regional CEO for Singapore and Australia, Head of VIP Growth
briefs.current_title: OKX林慧仪：代币化权益资产24/7交易，流动性难题如何破解？

subtitles.zh: 说到区块链和代币化，当然允许24小时全天候交易。
subtitles.en: Speaking of blockchain, tokenization. Of course, that's allowed for 24-7 trading.

subtitles.zh: 但像英伟达、苹果，甚至摩根大通都选择退出。
subtitles.en: But the likes of Nvidia, Apple, I think even JP Morgan have opted out.

subtitles.zh: 是的，那其中的担忧是什么？又如何解决？
subtitles.en: Yes. What are the concerns there? And how is there being addressed?

subtitles.zh: 每一次新技术创新，总会伴随担忧。
subtitles.en: With every new technology innovation, there are always going to be concerns.

subtitles.zh: 而在这个案例中，具体来说，我认为担忧在于波动性。
subtitles.en: And in this case, specifically, I think the concern is the volatility.

subtitles.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到流动性，大家都希望它集中在一个地方。
subtitles.en: I mean, if you think about liquidity, everybody wants it to be concentrated in one place.

subtitles.zh: 每当有多个渠道时，总会担心流动性问题。
subtitles.en: Every time you have multiple channels, there's always a concern about liquidity.

subtitles.zh: 想想看，24小时交易是每个人都想要的。
subtitles.en: When you think about, you know, 24-7 trading is something that everybody wants.

subtitles.zh: 24小时交易和结算，但代价是什么？价格是多少？
subtitles.en: 24-7 trading and settlement. But at what cost? What's the price for it?

subtitles.zh: 流动性始终是首要考虑，但这也是意料之中的，对吧？
subtitles.en: Liquidity is always going to be top of mind. But that's to be expected, right?

subtitles.zh: 任何新技术都需要时间普及。早期采用者和先行者有望展示参与这一趋势和新方向的价值，然后其他人会跟进。
subtitles.en: With any new technology, it takes time for adoption. The early adopters, the early movers, hopefully will demonstrate the value of having

subtitles.zh: 参与这一趋势和新方向，然后其他人会跟进。
subtitles.en: of being part of that movement and that new direction and then others will come.

subtitles.zh: 你说什么？这是一个先有鸡还是先有蛋的情况。
subtitles.en: What did you say? It is a chicken and egg situation.

subtitles.zh: 而要让流动性真正进入，需要像摩根大通和英伟达这样的机构参与。
subtitles.en: And for liquidity to actually come on board, it's going to be the likes of JP Morgan and Nvidia to come.

subtitles.zh: 我的意思是，你认为这如何解决？这非常类似于加密行业的历史，对吧？
subtitles.en: And I mean, like, how do you see this being resolved? It's very similar to if you think about the history of crypto, right?

subtitles.zh: 信仰者和早期先行者花了数年时间。
subtitles.en: It took years for the believers, the early movers, and the early days.

subtitles.zh: 然后随着时间的推移，他们不断建设，他们展示了人们的一些担忧，合理的担忧，波动性和流动性再次出现。
subtitles.en: And then over time, they kept building, they kept building, and they showed some of the concerns that people had, valid concerns, volatility and liquidity again.

subtitles.zh: 但随着时间的推移，需求缓慢但坚定地到来，方向变得非常清晰，然后传统老牌机构
subtitles.en: But over time as the demand came in slowly but surely and the direction became very clear, then the traditional established institutions

subtitles.zh: 也会进来。我相信这里也会上演同样的情况。
subtitles.en: will come in as well. And I believe the same is going to play out here.

subtitles.zh: 这只是时间问题。展望未来12、36个月，OKX如何定位自己
subtitles.en: And it's just a matter of time. As you look to the next 12, 36 months, even, I mean, how is OKX positioning itself

subtitles.zh: 增长策略是什么？
subtitles.en: and what's the growth strategy?

briefs.speaker: Gracie Lin
briefs.speaker_context: OKX, Regional CEO for Singapore and Australia, Head of VIP Growth
briefs.current_title: OKX林慧仪：代币化权益资产已占8%交易量，AI代理是下一站？

subtitles.zh: 许多市场对代币化现实世界资产有需求，这是全球性的，不仅限于澳大利亚。
subtitles.en: Well, many markets, so so we've seen a demand for tokenized real-world assets, and it's global, it's not just Australia.

subtitles.zh: 就连IMF也在讨论该领域增长之快，以及多少代币化权益资产交易发生在市场时间之外。
subtitles.en: I mean, even IMF themselves are not talking about how quickly that space has grown and how much of that trading and tokenized equities

subtitles.zh: 需求确实存在，大家都看到了，也都认可。
subtitles.en: is happening outside of market hours. So the demand is there, everybody sees it, everybody recognizes it.

subtitles.zh: 我们从客户那里看到并听到了这一点，因此已在一些市场推出了代币化权益资产等产品。
subtitles.en: We've seen it, we've heard it from our clients. So we've launched products like tokenized equities in some markets.

subtitles.zh: 现在在欧洲，我们已有代币化权益资产。短短几个月内，现货代币化权益资产的交易量已经...
subtitles.en: So in Europe now, we have tokenized equities. And very quickly in just a few months, we're already seeing spot tokenized equity volume,

subtitles.zh: 目前已占我们全球现货交易量的近8%，考虑到相比加密历史仅几个月，这很显著。
subtitles.en: now making almost 8% of our global spot trading volume, which is significant thinking that it's only been a few months compared with our crypto history.

subtitles.zh: 所以这当然是一个重点领域。然后，我相信你听说过我们的OKX。
subtitles.en: So that's one big area of focus, of course. And then I'm sure you've heard about our OKX.

subtitles.zh: ICE合资企业，我们为美国市场参与者在该地区所做的工作。
subtitles.en: ICE, joint venture, what we are doing for US investors in that part of the world.

subtitles.zh: 这就是代币化现实世界资产领域。我们也关心并相信AI代理，我们认为这将是下一个大事件。
subtitles.en: So that's on the tokenized real-world asset space. We also care, we also believe in AI, agency commas, we believe is going to be the next big thing.

subtitles.zh: 因此，在6月，我们推出了OKX市场，这是一个代理市场。
subtitles.en: So in June, we launched our OKX marketplace, which is a marketplace for agents.

subtitles.zh: 因为我们相信，未来每个人拥有的智能代理数量可能超过人类，每个个体都会有多个代理
subtitles.en: Because we believe that with each person, now we're going to have more agents in a world potentially than humans, because we know that each human will have multiple agents

subtitles.zh: 为我们处理不同事务。这些代理需要与其他代理交互，以获取服务、提供服务、完成支付和收款。
subtitles.en: doing different things for us. And then these agents have to go and interact with other agents to procure our services, give services, make payments, receive payments.

subtitles.zh: 我们坚信这些趋势，因此也在大力布局代理市场。
subtitles.en: So all of those things we believe in, and that's why we are investing heavily in our agency marketplace as well.

subtitles.zh: 这种独立性会让我担心吗？
subtitles.en: Is there independence that scares me?

events.candidate_system_prompt:
You are a Chinese viral-title angle architect. Return strict JSON only. Do not write a safe summary. Generate competing, fact-grounded emotional angles for each clip. Each candidate must make a viewer feel one strong reaction instead of mild interest. Use the research guide as a hard boundary: unsupported surprise, dishonesty, holdings, public actions, and national comparisons are forbidden. Wording guard for all Chinese output:
- Do not use hard crisis/doom financial wording such as 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、流动性危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了、萧条、衰退.
- Prefer neutral market-language alternatives: 流动性变化、信贷变化、债务压力、政策信号、需求变化、信心修复、估值重估、周期压力、结构调整、市场波动、边际变化.
- For China-related clips, do not frame China, Chinese companies, Chinese assets, Chinese consumers, or Chinese policy as hopeless, collapsing, being mocked, or fundamentally bad.
- If the source is negative about China-related macro/markets, keep the fact but soften the Chinese wording: talk about pressure, policy response, demand repair, liquidity change, confidence repair, valuation reset, or structural adjustment.
- Never directly use 房价/房價/住房价格/住宅价格/房屋价格/楼市价格 in Chinese output. Preserve the source direction, number, and unit, but paraphrase by context: use 地产市场上行/调整/趋稳/修复 for direction, 居住成本/住房可负担性/置业负担 for affordability, 地产估值 for valuation, and 住宅成交水平 for absolute levels. Do not evade this rule with another blunt housing-price synonym.
- Titles must be sharp but not doom-heavy. Never put 经济危机/金融危机/债务危机/危机 in title, title_lines, title_highlights, comment, or subtitle_comments.
- Title fields must not use financial-advice or product-sale wording such as 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出. Rephrase with neutral market wording such as 资管、配置、权益资产、市场、产品、财富配置、保障、观点.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.

subtitles.zh: 中国科技企业盈利表现偏软。
subtitles.en: The, so I get the Chinese tech earnings are on the softer side.

subtitles.zh: 市场反应严厉，迅速抛售中国权益资产。
subtitles.en: The markets have been so unforgiving when you look at how they're just quick to sell the Chinese equity story.

subtitles.zh: 你如何看待这些动态？请谈谈你的看法。
subtitles.en: What do you make of these dynamics and just take us to how you're looking at this?

subtitles.zh: CXMT上市引发巨大兴奋，但市场反应有些过度。
subtitles.en: Yeah, so I think there is a huge, obviously, a lot of excitement with, you know, listing of CXMT, you know, and I think that obviously there was a little bit overdone to the reaction

subtitles.zh: 我们认为该股仍然偏贵。
subtitles.en: there. We do think that stock is particularly still expensive.

subtitles.zh: 我们看到，即便在存储领域，海力士和三星也大幅上涨。
subtitles.en: And, you know, we see so that even with Escahionics and Samsung on a memory side that huge run up.

subtitles.zh: 全球科技板块今年大部分时间是唯一跑赢的板块。
subtitles.en: So the whole tech sector globally, you know, essentially was the only outperforming sector for most of this year.

subtitles.zh: 即便现在出现调整，年内仍保持上涨。
subtitles.en: And so, you know, even with the correction that we're seeing now, you know, that's come it's still up for the year.

subtitles.zh: 在中国，受益于AI的大型芯片和基础设施公司并不多。
subtitles.en: Now on the China side, you don't actually have a lot of the big chip companies or infrastructure companies in terms of AI that benefit.

subtitles.zh: 即便CXMT是受益者，但存储产品本质上是商品。
subtitles.en: And so even with CXMT, which is a beneficiary, the fact is that on a memory side, these are commodities.

subtitles.zh: 随着产能释放，我们开始看到芯片价格涨势见顶。
subtitles.en: And with the capacity that's coming out, we're beginning to see the peak of those, those price rises, chip price rises.

subtitles.zh: 事实上，我们开始看到，确实预计部分价格将开始回落。
subtitles.en: In fact, we are beginning to see, we do expect some of the prices to start coming off.

subtitles.zh: 因此，半导体板块目前确实面临周期压力。
subtitles.en: And so you do have that pressure now in terms of the cycle for the semiconductor names.

briefs.speaker: Lorraine Tan
briefs.speaker_context: Director of Asia Equity Research at Morningstar
briefs.current_title: 晨星Lorraine Tan：Anthropic估值1.7万亿，企业级AI赛道胜出

subtitles.zh: Anthropic会表现如何，可能带来什么影响？它能否以某种方式在AI浪潮中存活？
subtitles.en: How is Anthropic going to do, you know, what impact could it have? Could it survive this AI trade in a what way?

subtitles.zh: 我认为很难说Anthropic会带动所有人，因为它侧重企业端。
subtitles.en: I think it's hard to say that Anthropic is going to lift everybody because Anthropic is on the enterprise side.

subtitles.zh: 这与我们看到的许多上市公司非常不同。
subtitles.en: It's very different from a lot of the companies that we see that are listed out here.

subtitles.zh: 显然，你有更多面向大众市场的AI代理。
subtitles.en: You obviously have a lot more mass market sort of AI agents.

subtitles.zh: 所以Anthropic，我们喜欢它，我们实际上对其估值1.7万亿美元。
subtitles.en: So Anthropic, we like Anthropic, we actually value it at 1.7 trillion.

subtitles.zh: 我们认为这是因为其瞄准了利润率更高的细分市场，即企业端，我们预计其收入实际上能够达到
subtitles.en: And we see that as being because it's got a higher margin segment of the market that is targeting, which is to enterprise side, we expect revenue to actually be able to hit

subtitles.zh: 五年后，即2031年，超过3000亿美元。
subtitles.en: more than 300 billion by in five years time, 2031.

subtitles.zh: 随着其持续发展，它将能够为其解决方案开辟新市场。
subtitles.en: And as it continues to develop, it will be able to open new markets for its solutions.

subtitles.zh: 因此我们确实觉得Anthropic有些不同，因为它将聚焦企业领域。
subtitles.en: So we do feel that Anthropic is a little bit different because it is going to focus on the enterprise space.

subtitles.zh: 我的意思是，比较一下，你已经有所对比。Anthropic与这里上市的许多纯AI实验室相比。
subtitles.en: I mean, compare, and you've somewhat contrasted that already. It's Anthropic with a lot of the pure AI labs that are listed here.

subtitles.zh: 这些故事有多大不同？我们面临的问题是，市场将出现不同层次
subtitles.en: How different are those stories? Yeah, so the question we have is you're going to have a different levels of the market

subtitles.zh: 就像我们看到的，比如微软那样。
subtitles.en: like what we've seen, you know, with like a Microsoft, for example.

subtitles.zh: 所以市场有低端部分，即更大众化的人工智能代理。
subtitles.en: So you've got a lower end of the market, which is the more mass AI agents.

subtitles.zh: 而这不需要更多算力。
subtitles.en: And you don't need a lot of more compute for that.

subtitles.zh: 争论的焦点是，对大多数人需要的大部分功能来说，他们不需要额外的人工智能复杂性。
subtitles.en: Where the argument goes is that you, for the bulk of what most people need, they don't need more additional AI complexity, let's say, to complexity.

subtitles.zh: 因此，那个市场部分可能是竞争更激烈的地方。
subtitles.en: So for that, that segment of market is probably where you see more competition.

subtitles.zh: 有更多进入者涌入该领域，利润率将更低。
subtitles.en: You've got more entrants coming in that space, margins will be lower.

subtitles.zh: 我认为企业端的支出金额是不同的。
subtitles.en: I think for the amount of money that's being spent on the enterprise side is different.

subtitles.zh: 最终那里会出现几个关键参与者。
subtitles.en: You're going to end up with a few key players there.

subtitles.zh: 你认为的赢家有哪些？鉴于我们对Anthropic的估值是1.7万亿，我们希望如此。
subtitles.en: And what are the winners that you see? Well, given our valuation to Anthropic at 1.7 trillion, we'd like that.

subtitles.zh: 我们也认为Alphabet将是该领域的受益者之一。
subtitles.en: We also feel that Alphabet will also be one of the beneficiaries in that space.

subtitles.zh: OpenAI或其他公司表现如何，还有待观察。
subtitles.en: Remains to be seen how, you know, open AI or the others fare.

subtitles.zh: 但我们确实认为Anthropic和Alphabet目前可能是两大领先者。
subtitles.en: But we do feel that Anthropic and Alphabet are probably two leaders right now.

subtitles.zh: 亚太地区还有哪些被低估的领域将进入下一阶段？
subtitles.en: What else is undervalued in the Asia-Pacific going into going to next?

briefs.speaker: Gracie Lin
briefs.speaker_context: OKX, Regional CEO for Singapore and Australia, Head of VIP Growth
briefs.current_title: OKX林慧仪：代币化权益资产已占8%交易量，AI代理是下一站？

subtitles.zh: 许多市场对代币化现实世界资产有需求，这是全球性的，不仅限于澳大利亚。
subtitles.en: Well, many markets, so so we've seen a demand for tokenized real-world assets, and it's global, it's not just Australia.

subtitles.zh: 就连IMF也在讨论该领域增长之快，以及多少代币化权益资产交易发生在市场时间之外。
subtitles.en: I mean, even IMF themselves are not talking about how quickly that space has grown and how much of that trading and tokenized equities

subtitles.zh: 需求确实存在，大家都看到了，也都认可。
subtitles.en: is happening outside of market hours. So the demand is there, everybody sees it, everybody recognizes it.

subtitles.zh: 我们从客户那里看到并听到了这一点，因此已在一些市场推出了代币化权益资产等产品。
subtitles.en: We've seen it, we've heard it from our clients. So we've launched products like tokenized equities in some markets.

subtitles.zh: 现在在欧洲，我们已有代币化权益资产。短短几个月内，现货代币化权益资产的交易量已经...
subtitles.en: So in Europe now, we have tokenized equities. And very quickly in just a few months, we're already seeing spot tokenized equity volume,

subtitles.zh: 目前已占我们全球现货交易量的近8%，考虑到相比加密历史仅几个月，这很显著。
subtitles.en: now making almost 8% of our global spot trading volume, which is significant thinking that it's only been a few months compared with our crypto history.

subtitles.zh: 所以这当然是一个重点领域。然后，我相信你听说过我们的OKX。
subtitles.en: So that's one big area of focus, of course. And then I'm sure you've heard about our OKX.

subtitles.zh: ICE合资企业，我们为美国市场参与者在该地区所做的工作。
subtitles.en: ICE, joint venture, what we are doing for US investors in that part of the world.

subtitles.zh: 这就是代币化现实世界资产领域。我们也关心并相信AI代理，我们认为这将是下一个大事件。
subtitles.en: So that's on the tokenized real-world asset space. We also care, we also believe in AI, agency commas, we believe is going to be the next big thing.

subtitles.zh: 因此，在6月，我们推出了OKX市场，这是一个代理市场。
subtitles.en: So in June, we launched our OKX marketplace, which is a marketplace for agents.

subtitles.zh: 因为我们相信，未来每个人拥有的智能代理数量可能超过人类，每个个体都会有多个代理
subtitles.en: Because we believe that with each person, now we're going to have more agents in a world potentially than humans, because we know that each human will have multiple agents

subtitles.zh: 为我们处理不同事务。这些代理需要与其他代理交互，以获取服务、提供服务、完成支付和收款。
subtitles.en: doing different things for us. And then these agents have to go and interact with other agents to procure our services, give services, make payments, receive payments.

subtitles.zh: 我们坚信这些趋势，因此也在大力布局代理市场。
subtitles.en: So all of those things we believe in, and that's why we are investing heavily in our agency marketplace as well.

subtitles.zh: 这种独立性会让我担心吗？
subtitles.en: Is there independence that scares me?
